strategy.bottleneck: [latency/utilisation-imbalance across a serial dependency chain] The forward is one strictly serial stream: cuDNN `sm90_xmma_fprop_implicit_gemm...nhwc` (63.1%, 7147us, ~68% of TF32 peak, only ~0.45-0.67 TB/s DRAM) alternating with four DRAM-bound custom kernels (gn_silu_res_t 12.2%, gn_partial 9.0%, nchw2nhwc 7.3%, gn_silu 6.5%) that sit at 73-81% DRAM but 20-45% SM. Tensor cores idle during GN, DRAM idles during conv.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Batch-split stream pipelining: split the block along N (exact, no halo, GN stats are per-(n,group)) into chunks and run convolutions on one CUDA stream and all GroupNorm/SiLU/transpose kernels on a second, with events creating a one-stage skew so conv of chunk i+1 overlaps GN of chunk i. Metrics justify it: memory-bound kernels already run at 81% DRAM (no per-kernel headroom, bytes are compulsory), while the compute-bound conv leaves DRAM ~70% idle; only concurrency can recover the ~347us/iter of serial memory time.
strategy.modification_plan:
Only the host schedule inside `fused_block` changes; all five __global__ kernels stay byte-identical (guarantees numerics).

1. EXACT CODE ACTION — chunking: after computing N,C,H,W, add `int k = (N >= 4) ? 4 : (int)N;` and per-chunk ranges `n0 = c*((N+k-1)/k)`, `cn = min(chunk, N-n0)` (skip empty chunks so odd N works). Build per-chunk views with `.narrow(0,n0,cn)` on x_cl, y1, z, y2, out, xc — batch is the outermost dim in both NCHW and NHWC so every narrow stays contiguous in its memory format. If `N < 2`, execute the existing single-stream path unchanged (protects the 1x256x131x131 shape, currently 2.06x).

2. EXACT CODE ACTION — two streams + events: `auto sC = at::cuda::getStreamFromPool(); auto sM = at::cuda::getStreamFromPool();` (function-local `static thread_local` so streams are created once). Record `at::cuda::CUDAEvent ev0` on the current stream after the K1 nchw2nhwc launches and have both sC and sM `block()` on it, so side streams see x_cl. Allocate arrays `CUDAEvent evConv1[k], evGN1[k], evConv2[k], evGN2[k]`. Wrap every launch in `at::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard g(stream);` and replace `at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()` in the raw launches with the guarded stream so at::conv2d and the custom kernels land on the intended stream.

3. Issue order (this is what creates the skew — do not issue per-chunk chains):
   sC: for c in 0..k-1 { conv1(chunk c); evConv1[c].record(sC); }
   sM: for c { evConv1[c].block(sM); gn_partial/gn_finalize/gn_silu(chunk c); evGN1[c].record(sM); }
   sC: for c { evGN1[c].block(sC); conv2(chunk c); evConv2[c].record(sC); }
   sM: for c { evConv2[c].block(sM); gn_partial/gn_finalize/gn_silu_res_t(chunk c); evGN2[c].record(sM); }
   Result: conv1(c1..c3) runs concurrently with GN1(c0); conv2(c0..) runs concurrently with GN1(c1..).

4. Buffer disjointness: index `part`, `scale`, `shift` with a per-chunk offset (`part.data_ptr<double>() + (size_t)n0*GG*nchunks*2`, `scale.data_ptr<float>() + n0*CC`) and pass `blockIdx.y`-local n as today. All GN kernels live on sM, so norm1's apply for chunk c always precedes norm2's finalize for any chunk in stream order — no WAR hazard; the offsets remove any doubt.

5. Allocator safety: for every tensor created on the current stream but consumed on sC/sM (x_cl, y1, z, y2, out, part, scale, shift, w1c, w2c), call `c10::cuda::CUDACachingAllocator::recordStream(t.storage().data_ptr(), sC/sM)` to prevent premature block reuse.

6. Join: at the end, `evGN2[k-1].block(getCurrentCUDAStream())` and also block on `evConv2[k-1]`, then return `out`. The returned tensor is thus safe for the caller's stream and the harness's event timing stays valid.

7. Keep `nchunks/ppc` reduction schedule but recompute the block target from per-chunk work: `nc = ceil(8*sms / cn)` clamped as today, so the stats grid still fills the SM while sharing the GPU with a concurrent conv.

8. Guardrail on chunk size: require per-chunk implicit-GEMM M = cn*H*W >= 8192; otherwise reduce k (k=2 or 1). For 8x64x128 with k=4 each conv still issues ~512 CTAs (4.5 waves), so tail-wave loss stays under ~5%.

9. Validate all four shapes; ensure the N=1 shape takes the untouched single-stream path and that outputs are bitwise identical to the current candidate (same kernels, same reduction order per sample).

DELTA vs Previous Attempt #2: keep its single-stream full-forward capture and its unchanged plan_chunk, but REPLACE the `const float* const*` global pointer-buffer arguments in K1/K5 with `__constant__` symbols. Attempt #2's indirection pushed gn_silu_res_t from 31 to 34 regs, occupancy_limit_registers 8->6, theoretical occupancy 100%->75%; __constant__ reads are uniform, resolve in the constant bank like kernel params, and must restore 31 regs.
2. Add at file scope: `struct IOPtrs { const float* x; float* out; };  __constant__ IOPtrs c_io;` and `__constant__ float c_gn[4*256];` (n1w,n1b,n2w,n2b at float offsets 0,256,512,768).
3. Change `nchw2nhwc_kernel` signature to `(float* dst, long elem_off, int HW)`; first line `const float* s = c_io.x + elem_off + (size_t)n*CC*HW;`. Keep body, block (32,8), grid ((HW+31)/32, C/32, chunk), shared tile[32][33] and the `p < HW` guard unchanged.
4. Change `gn_silu_res_t_kernel` signature to `(const float* y, const float* scale, const float* shift, long elem_off, int HW)`; inside use `const float* xres = c_io.x + elem_off;` and `float* out = c_io.out + elem_off;`. Keep grid/block/tile and `p < HW` guard unchanged.
5. Change `gn_finalize_kernel` to take `int which` instead of the gamma/beta pointers; inside: `const float* gamma = c_gn + (which?512:0); const float* beta = c_gn + (which?768:256);`.
6. Host helper `set_io_ptrs(x, out)`: write the two pointers into a once-allocated 16-byte pinned host buffer and `cudaMemcpyToSymbolAsync(c_io, host, 16, 0, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, current_stream)`. Runs OUTSIDE the graph.
7. Host helper `set_gn_params(n1w,n1b,n2w,n2b)`: four `cudaMemcpyToSymbolAsync(c_gn, t.data_ptr(), 1024, offset, cudaMemcpyDeviceToDevice, current_stream)` calls (offsets 0,1024,2048,3072 bytes). This replaces four `.copy_()` elementwise kernels per forward with DMA.
8. Add C++ `full_pipeline(w1c,w2c,eps,part,scale,shift,x_cl,z,nchunks,ppc,M,N,chunk,C,H,W)` enqueuing on the CURRENT stream, for off=0,chunk,2*chunk,...: K1(x_cl, off*C*HW) -> at::cudnn_convolution(benchmark=true, allow_tf32=true, NHWC) -> gn_partial -> gn_finalize(which=0) -> gn_silu -> conv2 -> gn_partial -> gn_finalize(which=1) -> K5(y2, scale, shift, off*C*HW). No syncs, no host allocations.
9. Keep plan_chunk EXACTLY as-is (target_live 40MB, guard chunk*HW<16384, snap-to-divisor) so l2_resident_batch_blocking survives; keep set_l2_window(z) on the capture stream when chunk<N.
10. Warmup: run full_pipeline 3x on a side stream, torch.cuda.synchronize(), then capture once per (shape,dtype,device,eps) key with a fresh graph_pool_handle(); keep the 8-entry cache and try/except falling back to the existing interior-graph path, then fused_block.
11. forward(): `st['w1c'].copy_(conv1_weight); st['w2c'].copy_(conv2_weight); ext.set_gn_params(...); out = torch.empty(xc.shape,...); ext.set_io_ptrs(xc, out); g.replay(); return out`. Delete the Python chunk loop.
12. Verify after build that K5 reports launch__registers_per_thread <= 31 and theoretical occupancy 100%; if not, add `__launch_bounds__(256, 8)` to K5.
strategy.evidence: Failure class of Previous Attempt #2 = (b): its anti-regression clause explicitly required K1/K5 to keep launch__registers_per_thread 28/31, but the measured rejected profile shows gn_silu_res_t at 34 regs, launch__occupancy_limit_registers 6 (base 8), Theoretical Occupancy 75.0% (base 100.0%), achieved 63.55% vs base 80.97%, and gpu__time_duration 69216ns vs base 65728ns (+5.3%) — the launch-count saving was eaten by a per-kernel slowdown caused by the global pointer indirection, so the mechanism was defective, not the target. Its per-shape line (+1.4% on 8x256x64x128, -4.4%/-4.6% on the two NC=1 shapes) is consistent with that per-kernel cost dominating wherever there are few chunks. Base numbers justifying the target: nsys shows gn_silu_res_t 24.6% (2422us, 48 launches) + nchw2nhwc 21.8% (2148us, 48 launches) = 46.4% of forward GPU time, with sm__throughput only 15.75%/21.92% and gpu__dram_throughput 32.65%/34.18% of peak, and 190 total launches per forward. Section analysis (SpeedOfLight, nchw2nhwc): 'low compute throughput and memory bandwidth utilization ... below 60.0% of peak typically indicate latency issues.' Ruled out as #1: register/occupancy pressure in the BASE kernels — sm__warps_active 87.29% (K1) and 83.32% (K5) of peak at 28/31 regs with smsp__sass_branch_targets_threads_divergent 0.0, so adding warps cannot be the fix; also ruled out gn_finalize (sm__throughput 1.45%, waves_per_multiprocessor 0.04) as negligible. This plan COMPOSES: cudnn_algo_autotune stays (cudnn_convolution benchmark/TF32/NHWC inside full_pipeline), l2_resident_batch_blocking stays (plan_chunk and the chunk loop untouched, now inside the graph), and the existing interior capture is extended, not removed.
strategy.expected_metric_change: (1) Per-forward CPU enqueues drop from ~190 to 1 graph replay + 2 weight copies + 5 async symbol memcpys -> end-to-end time down, largest on the launch-sensitive 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131 shapes that Attempt #2 regressed. (2) sm__cycles_elapsed/sm__cycles_active gap shrinks: nchw2nhwc 47239/30478 (1.55) toward ~1.1 and gn_silu_res_t 71898/57635 (1.25) toward ~1.05, i.e. inter-kernel bubbles removed. Anti-regression (the metrics that would expose failure): (a) gn_silu_res_t MUST keep launch__registers_per_thread <= 31, launch__occupancy_limit_registers 8, Theoretical Occupancy 100% and gpu__time_duration <= 65728ns — this is exactly what Attempt #2 broke; (b) nchw2nhwc must keep launch__grid_size 4096, block 256, shared_mem_per_block 5248 and regs <= 28; (c) l2_resident_batch_blocking must stay alive: gn_partial launch__waves_per_multiprocessor 0.56 and achieved occupancy >= 51%, gn_silu lts__t_sector_hit_rate ~51%; (d) cudnn_algo_autotune must stay: sm90_xmma_fprop_implicit_gemm_*_nhwckrsc_nhwc engines still in the timeline, no reappearance of the sm80 nchw fprop or extra convertTensor_kernel; (e) total DRAM bytes must NOT increase — no static_x/static_out full-tensor copies (the defect of Attempt #1); (f) exactly one capture per shape key, and 1x256x131x131 (HW=17161) must stay bit-correct via the untouched p<HW guards.
